overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of the debate over AI in education and the evidence behind it. You'll be asked about survey evidence on use, institutional guidance, the difference between performance and learning, and the three main positions.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: In a national survey, 49 percent of undergraduates said AI had improved their experience as students. What does this result show?

options.html: About half of the students learned more because of AI tools
options.text: About half of the students learned more because of AI tools
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A survey doesn't test what students can do. The result shows how about half of the students said they felt about AI.

options.html: How about half of the students said they felt about AI
options.text: How about half of the students said they felt about AI
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Surveys rest on self-report. They show reported behavior and attitudes, and they don't measure learning.

options.html: AI tools raised the grades of about half of the students
options.text: AI tools raised the grades of about half of the students
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The survey didn't measure grades. The result shows how about half of the students said they felt about AI.

options.html: About half of the students used AI in their assessed work
options.text: About half of the students used AI in their assessed work
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That was a separate question with a much higher figure. This result shows how about half of the students said they felt about AI.

forms.stemHtml: UNESCO's 2023 guidance says the minimum age for independent conversations with generative AI platforms should be 13. What is the status of that statement?

options.html: A law that applies in every member country of the United Nations
options.text: A law that applies in every member country of the United Nations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. UNESCO can't make law for any country. The statement is a recommendation to governments, which decide for themselves.

options.html: A rule that schools must follow to keep their public funding
options.text: A rule that schools must follow to keep their public funding
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The guidance has no authority over schools or their funding. The statement is a recommendation to governments, which decide for themselves.

options.html: A finding from research on how chatbots affect young children
options.text: A finding from research on how chatbots affect young children
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The guidance takes the number from existing company terms and an older privacy law. The statement is a recommendation to governments, which decide for themselves.

options.html: A recommendation to governments, which decide for themselves
options.text: A recommendation to governments, which decide for themselves
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The guidance is advice to member countries. Each country decides the actual age, how it is verified, and who is accountable.

forms.stemHtml: In a field experiment, high school students who practiced mathematics with an ordinary chatbot scored higher during practice than students with no AI, and lower on a later exam taken without AI. What does this show?

options.html: AI raised their performance and lowered their learning
options.text: AI raised their performance and lowered their learning
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Performance is how well a student does with help available. Learning is what remains without it. The chatbot improved the first and harmed the second.

options.html: AI raised their learning and lowered their performance
options.text: AI raised their learning and lowered their performance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This reverses the two. Practice scores with help are performance, and the unassisted exam shows learning. AI raised their performance and lowered their learning.

options.html: AI had no measurable effect on these students either way
options.text: AI had no measurable effect on these students either way
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both scores changed. AI raised their performance during practice and lowered their learning, as shown by the later exam.

options.html: AI helps in mathematics and harms in every other subject
options.text: AI helps in mathematics and harms in every other subject
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The experiment covered one subject and can't be extended to others. It showed that AI raised their performance and lowered their learning.

forms.stemHtml: A trial in a university physics course found that students learned more in less time with an AI tutor than in an active-learning class. Which statements about this trial are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The tutor was purpose-built by the researchers for that course
options.text: The tutor was purpose-built by the researchers for that course
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The design of the tutor, including step-by-step solutions written into its instructions, was the point of the study.

options.html: It shows that giving students any chatbot improves their learning
options.text: It shows that giving students any chatbot improves their learning
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The trial tested one carefully designed tutor. A separate experiment found that an ordinary chatbot lowered later exam scores.

options.html: It covered one subject at one university over a short period
options.text: It covered one subject at one university over a short period
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Whether the result holds in other subjects, for other ages, or over years hasn't been tested.

options.html: Advocates of AI as a tutor for every student cite it as support
options.text: Advocates of AI as a tutor for every student cite it as support
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It is the main experimental evidence for that position.

forms.stemHtml: Which statement best expresses the assessment-reform position on AI in education?

options.html: AI tools should be banned so that existing assignments still work
options.text: AI tools should be banned so that existing assignments still work
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The position holds that a ban leaves a broken measurement in place. It says that if AI can complete a task, the task should change.

options.html: AI tutors should replace classroom teaching in most subjects
options.text: AI tutors should replace classroom teaching in most subjects
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That goes beyond even the tutor position. The assessment-reform position says that if AI can complete a task, the task should change.

options.html: If AI can complete a task, the task itself should change
options.text: If AI can complete a task, the task itself should change
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An assessment that a chatbot can complete no longer shows what the student knows. Advocates propose tasks that reveal a student's own thinking.

options.html: Students should be graded on how well they can prompt a chatbot
options.text: Students should be graded on how well they can prompt a chatbot
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The position is about making assessments show a student's own learning. It says that if AI can complete a task, the task should change.

title: AI in schools and universities
